blocks.text: Receptors are organs, tissues, cells or parts of cells that detect changes (stimuli) in the external or internal environment and create nerve impulses in their sensory neurons. The following topics describe the receptors for taste, smell, touch and pain.

blocks.title: Free nerve endings
blocks.text: The simplest receptors are free nerve endings, which respond to stimuli such as changes in temperature or chemicals in the extracellular fluid.

blocks.prompt: What do all receptors do with a stimulus?
blocks.explanation: They detect it and turn it into nerve impulses in their sensory neurons (they act as transducers).

items: Receptors detect stimuli and create impulses in sensory neurons; free nerve endings are the simplest.
